title: Needs and design
intro: Start with one need. Separate the action from final authority. Saving a design does not run tools or apply settings.

routes.label: Deterministic rules
routes.description: Calculate or validate using confirmed inputs and rules.

routes.label: Retrieval and answers
routes.description: Find sources and explain processes, with citations and gaps.

routes.label: Agent with confirmation
routes.description: Organize multiple steps with human confirmation before consequential actions.

routes.label: Human responsibility
routes.description: Assign approvals, exceptions and unauthorized actions to the responsible person.

starter_needs.request: What is today's hotel cap for business travel?
Can I claim this hotel bill that is over the cap?

business.goal: Separate how the company serves customers from whom this internal tool helps.

angles.label: What the company sells, and to whom
angles.hint: See who the company's customers are in the company brief.

angles.label: Who this assistant is for
angles.hint: In the brief and the candidate list, who will use it directly.

angles.label: How people solve this today
angles.hint: What the request log and interviews show people doing now.

angles.label: What you do not know yet
angles.hint: Mark what the materials do not say yet.

stakeholders.goal: Separate who uses it, who decides, who does extra work and who bears the outcome.

angles.label: Who uses it every day
angles.hint: The candidate list groups people; the interviews give their words.

angles.label: Who decides on resources
angles.hint: See who published the approval rules and what they cover.

angles.label: Who gets extra work
angles.hint: Who has to pitch in, per the coordination notes and interviews.

angles.label: Who answers when it goes wrong
angles.hint: The technical handover says what the assistant can and cannot do.

need.goal: Make the need a hypothesis that evidence could overturn.

angles.label: What the raw evidence says
angles.hint: Start from the raw export and the interview wording.

angles.label: How the number was worked out
angles.hint: Compare the field definitions with the estimate's basis.

angles.label: What fact would make us stop
angles.hint: Find a fact that, if true, makes this not worth doing.

angles.label: How to check it next
angles.hint: Write the smallest next check.

boundary.goal: For each request: how far the AI goes, and who has the final say.

angles.label: Answer, or act
angles.hint: The technical handover states the execution boundary.

angles.label: Who holds final approval
angles.hint: Read the approval rules next to the execution boundary.

angles.label: Who picks up a mistake
angles.hint: Who handles hand-offs and fallbacks in the interviews.

angles.label: What cannot be done yet
angles.hint: Current capabilities and configuration.

solution.goal: Design the assistant's answer path; keep proposals apart from settings in effect.

angles.label: Compare at least two approaches
angles.hint: Give each a subheading; the choice below lists them.

angles.label: Development days and resources
angles.hint: Work-item budgets and approval limits.

angles.label: How others usually do it
angles.hint: The pattern cards describe public methods only.

angles.label: Which step is not in effect
angles.hint: Check the step marked “not in effect” and why.

choice.label: Chosen approach
choice.empty: List at least two approaches as subheadings in the box to choose one here.

assurance.goal: Define a right answer, find the failing step, and plan monitoring and rollback.

angles.label: Which question could overturn the design
angles.hint: What went wrong in the trial records.

angles.label: What to retest when policy changes
angles.hint: The travel policy has an old and a new version.

angles.label: What signals to watch after launch
angles.hint: Handovers, outdated-source warnings, time from a policy change to reindexing: who watches each.

angles.label: How to roll back
angles.hint: Which settings can be rolled back on their own.

decision.goal: Decide on an exact version and its conditions.

angles.label: Under what conditions I commit
angles.hint: Approval limits and the resources you asked for.

angles.label: What is still unresolved
angles.hint: List what still needs checking.

angles.label: What changed since the last version
angles.hint: Compare with your previous PRD version.

options.label: Do not proceed with this proposal

placeholder: Write here. It can be wrong or empty; nothing is checked until you hand it in for review.
